LocationThis is a full-time position based at our HQ in Munich or Cologne.About the roleYou solve the hard technical problems on live systems.Once a customer is running on blp, their processes are business critical. Invoices post or they do not. Orders flow or they sit. Our support organisation resolves most of what comes in, and a lot of it is genuinely well handled by people early in their career. What is left is yours: the cases where the cause is not obvious, where it crosses systems, data and process logic at once, where the same symptom has three possible explanations and only one of them is right.That is the job. Not a queue, and not the easy half of one. Everything difficult that comes out of the run phase lands with you.Two things sit alongside the case work, and they are what make this a senior job rather than a harder version of a junior one.Stabilising accountsWhen an account's health goes bad, you go in and stabilise it. Not as a permanent assignment, but as a small, highly skilled squad that takes a customer whose numbers or whose confidence have slipped, works out what is actually wrong across the whole picture, fixes it, and hands back a customer who is running properly again. It is the most concentrated version of this work there is.Taking effort out permanentlyAnything that keeps arriving in the queue is a signal, and the answer is usually not more people answering it. It might be better self-service for customers, a customer-facing assistant that resolves the routine questions before they reach us, better diagnostics, or a change in how something is configured at deployment so the problem never occurs. You are expected to find those, make the case, and drive them through. That is how a support organisation scales without scaling headcount one for one, and it is value the customer feels directly.You work across the boundary between what our platform does, what the customer's ERP does, and what their data actually looks like. You are the one who can read a failing case end to end and say what really happened, and then say credibly whether the fix is configuration, data, process, or a genuine product issue. When it is a product issue, you are the counterpart to our engineering and product teams: you bring the evidence, and because you have seen the same structural problem across several customers, your case is the one that moves the roadmap.You are also how this function gets better rather than just bigger. The diagnostic tooling, the patterns, the documentation that lets a first-year person resolve what used to take a senior one: that is yours to build. And the interns and specialists coming through the team learn this craft from you.You do not deliver integrations and you do not run go-lives. Our integrations engineers and technical project managers own that. You own what happens once it is live and it is challenging.What you'll doOwn the technically difficult cases from our live customer base, end to end, to a verified root cause.Diagnose across boundaries: platform behaviour, ERP behaviour, master data and process logic.Decide what the real fix is, and make it: configuration, data, process, or a case for engineering.Go into accounts with a deteriorating health score, diagnose across the whole picture, stabilise them and hand them back running properly.Drive strategic initiatives that permanently reduce effort and improve the customer experience, from better diagnostics to customer-facing self-service and assistants.Act as the counterpart to Product and Engineering, with evidence strong enough to change priorities.Recognise structural problems across customers and push for them to be solved once.Build the diagnostic tooling, patterns and documentation that raise what the rest of the team can resolve alone.Mentor interns and earlier-career colleagues, and raise the technical bar of the function.Support Consultants and Customer Success Managers on the technical substance of customer escalations.What we're really looking forThe following key attributes ensure success in this role:Root Cause, Not Symptom – You are not finished when it stops happening. You are finished when you know why.Cross-Boundary Reasoning – You hold platform, ERP, data and process in your head at once and find where the truth is.Credible Both Ways – You explain the same problem to an engineer and to a CFO, and both of them believe you.Leverage – Your instinct is to remove the next hundred cases, not only to close this one. You would rather build the thing that makes a problem stop arriving.Calm Under Escalation – When a business-critical process is stopped, you get more precise rather than faster.Stabilizer Under Pressure: An unhappy client is not a fire to put out. It is a relationship to rebuild. You bring the temperature down, put structure back into the account, and align next steps so trust returns, not just silenceWhat you'll bringMaster's degree in a STEM field: computer science, engineering, information systems, mathematics, physics or similar. Strong candidates from a related field are welcome to make their case.3+ years in a technical customer-facing role: application support at depth, technical consulting, solution engineering, integration engineering or equivalent.Demonstrable debugging ability across systems, not only within one. APIs, data mapping, interfaces, logs.Comfortable with data. SQL or equivalent, and the instinct to check rather than assume.German and English, both fluent. This is a hard requirement. Our customers work in German every day and our internal work runs in English.Nice to have: ERP experience with SAP, Microsoft Dynamics or similar, scripting in any language, or exposure to workflow automation and process mining.What you'll getThe hard problems, not the queue.Influence on the product, with a direct line to Engineering and Product.Room to shape the function, since the practice is still being built.Real growth – the path from here leads into Consulting, technical leadership within Customer Success, or Product.Employee ownership – be part of a majority employee-owned company with a best-in-class stock option programme.Amazing team – become part of a driven and collaborative group of innovators.Visits &amp

column1: senior-product-manager-wealth-ai-berlin-27441,Getquin,"Senior Product Manager, Wealth & AI (f/m/d)",Berlin,False,1790410171,"What we doAt getquin, we're on a mission to empower everyone to build wealth.Founded in 2020, we started with a simple idea: help people see their entire financial life in one place, so they can make more informed decisions.Today, getquin has grown into one of the largest wealth platforms globally, already helping over half a million users manage and grow their wealth. Our platform combines analytics, tools and community to make wealth-building accessible for everyone, not just the experts.After launching in Germany, we've started expanding across Europe, with a focus on growing our user base, building valuable new features and helping even more people take control of their financial future.If you're excited to help shape the future of personal wealth management, join us. We're just getting started.What you'll be doingYou've built products for investors. You know what a TER actually does to a long-run return, why a user with four brokers has no visbility what they really own, and how differently people behave when the number on screen is their pension rather than their pocket money.You've probably also hit the ceiling of what a chart can tell someone. Better tables, more filters, another allocation donut. The data was always there
column2: the answer never quite arrived.We have something nobody else has: a complete, cross-institution picture of a person's wealth. Investments, cash, liabilities and insurance contracts, in one place, for over half a million users. Your work is turning that into features and insights people understand and act on, and the interesting tools for doing that now include AI.We're looking for an experienced Senior Product Manager to own that area. You'll work directly with the founders and the product team, alongside engineering and our financial advisory teams. This is a senior individual contributor role with no direct reports, and you'll mentor less experienced product managers on the team.Own the wealth product area end to endSet the product strategy and roadmap across the picture we give people of their wealth and how we help them optimize itDecide what we build on aggregated portfolio data that nobody with a single-broker view could build at allOwn our efforts to stay on the forefront of digital wealth management services and play your part in disrupting a still very offline industryWork the unglamorous, high-leverage problems too: data quality, coverage gaps, missing cost basis, duplicate holdings across connections, ETFs held through more than one broker. A portfolio insight is only as trustworthy as the numbers under itTurn the data into something users act onDefine the insights we surface about someone's portfolio, cash position and risk, and why each one earns a place on their screenOwn our conversational AI assistant and our AI-driven insights: what they say, what they refuse to say, and how a user knows which is whichSet the quality bar for anything we tell a user about their money: accuracy targets, human review, guardrails, rollback. Decide when something is good enough to ship and hold that line when the pressure is to ship anywayOwn the numbersDefine the metrics for your area: activation, engagement, the insight-to-action funnel, and contribution to subscription conversion and retentionRun the experiments, including proper A/B testing, read them, and report what didn't work alongside what didLive in your own product analytics and write your own queries and reporting, rather than wait for someone to give that to youWhat we are looking forYou might be a fit if:You've built wealth management, investing or portfolio products. You know the domain properly: instruments, ETFs, costs, allocation, risk, tax drag, and how retail investors actually behave rather than how they should. This is the requirement we're least flexible onYou've owned a product area end to end against a number you defined yourself, with real experimentation behind itYou've shipped at least one AI or LLM-based feature to production for real users, and you owned its output quality. You've shipped inside a legal or compliance constraint, and you can reason about where an insight becomes advice. Your product discovery produces evidence, not opinion. You can show us a real research artefact and a decision that changed because of itYou're fluent in English
column3: German is a plusYou can work from our Berlin office, and you already have the right to work in GermanyThat usually adds up to around five or more years in product, but we care about the evidence, not the year count. If you came to product from engineering, data science, research, design, financial services, or from a Product Owner role, that counts. Strong plus if you have:PSD2, open banking or account aggregation experienceInsurance or brokerage product exposure, which matters as we move into advisoryRecommendation systems or personalisation at scaleSubscription and paywall experimentationExperience mentoring or coaching other product managersYour own portfolio, and opinions about itIf you meet most of this and not all of it, apply. We'd rather read your application than guess.Work authorisationThis role requires an existing right to work in Germany. We're not able to sponsor visas or support relocation for this position, so we can only consider candidates who already hold German or EU work authorisation, or who can obtain it independently. We'd rather tell you now than after four conversations.What the first six months look likeMonth 1: you know the data model, the aggregation layer and its technology behind it. What our analytics do and don't cover, and understand how AI is already being used and where it. You've written down the three things you think are most wrong with the product todayMonths 2 to 3: a written, agreed area strategy with a prioritised roadmap, a primary metric with a baseline, and, clear metrics that you will be monitoring and optimizing along the wayMonths 3 to 4: the first thing you scoped is live to a user segment, with a read on the primary metric, and with quality measurement behind it if it involves generated outputMonths 5 to 6: two or three shipped iterations with measured results, including the ones that didn't work, a quality bar the team applies without you in the room, and at least one junior product manager who's visibly better at their job because of youYou won't be measured on shipping volume. You'll be measured on whether your area got measurably more useful and more trustworthy.Why join getquin?Why join getquin?We're a fast-growing B2C fintech, and here, your work has real impact. From day one, you'll take ownership of your domain, ship features end-to-end, and help shape the direction of a product used across Europe. We value initiative, ownership and creativity, not layers of process.Three things that are specifically true of this role:Wealth management is ripe for disruption. Following digitalisation waves of banking and brokerage services, we are leading those efforts across the next big topic for private individuals: better understand  and optimize your wealthThe data asset is genuinely rare. Aggregated cross-institution wealth for half a million people, with over +€25bn in connected assets. Trade Republic sees its own platform. N26 sees the current account. Nobody else in Europe sees the whole picture, which means there are product questions you can only answer hereYou'll own the area, not a slice of it. At our size the decisions are yoursReady to build something meaningful? Then join us at the forefront of making wealth building accessible to everyone.How we hireFive conversations, typically three to four weeks from first call to decision. We tell you where you stand after every step, and we respond within seven days at every stage.Recruiter screen, 30 min, video. Role, scope, the salary band, hybrid expectation, notice period, work authorisation. No trick questionsHiring manager, 60 min, video. Your product area ownership, the outcome you drove, and your depth in the wealth domain. This is the first real fit conversation, in both directionsProduct case, take home. We give you a real getquin problem on aggregated wealth data and work through it together. We know you already have a job, hence we do not impose an in-person case during working hoursCross-functional panel, 2 x 30 min, in our Berlin office. Cover in more depth your case study and deep dive further in your understanding of product metrics and approach to product development. Usually in person in our office.Close conversation, 30 min. Team fit, how you like to work, and whatever is still open, including your questions for a founderAlong the last part we will be making reference checks, but only with former employers. Once we have this, we will make you a formal offer. The whole loop runs in English. Tell us if you need any adjustment to the process, whether timing, format or accessibility, and we'll make it. You don't need to explain why.Find Jobs in Germany on Arbeitnow",['git'],1

column1: product-engineer-backend-ai-at-briink-berlin-413825,Merantix,Product Engineer (Backend/AI) @Briink,Berlin,False,1790399389,"What we doAt Briink, we’re building AI technology for the global sustainability economy. We work with the world’s largest climate organizations, including CDP and PRI, and multinational companies such as Bayer, Siemens, Commerzbank, E.ON, and Heidelberg Materials.Our technology helps automate how sustainability data is collected, analyzed, verified, and acted on. Through our work with global climate organizations, what you build at Briink will directly impact the sustainability workflows of more than 30,000 companies, investors, and cities worldwide.We’re a small team working at enormous scale. Your code won’t sit behind an internal tool or an experimental demo — it will help shape how some of the world’s largest organizations understand and act on their environmental impact. Based at Berlin’s AI Campus, with a second office in London, and backed by over €7 million in funding, we want to prove that some of the world’s most powerful technology can also be a powerful force for good.Application requirement: Intro videoAs part of your application, please submit a short intro video (max 2 minutes) answering:Who you are and what you have done/built that is relevant for this role. Why you’re excited about owning and shipping AI-powered products at Briink. Why Briink’s sustainability mission resonates with you.Upload your video using this form (YouTube unlisted, Loom, or any other solution is fine). We do this to get a better sense of candidates before continuing the process. Any application without a video will not be considered
column2: )Your roleAs Briink’s Backend/AI Product Engineer, you’ll join a small, high-ownership product and engineering team building AI-powered products for sustainability professionals.This is not a narrowly scoped backend role. You’ll take meaningful product problems from initial discovery and user conversations through technical design, implementation, and iteration to deploy them at scale across the ESG market. You’ll combine strong backend and AI/LLM engineering with product judgement and the initiative to work out what should be built - not just how to action a predefined ticket.You will:Own product features end to end, from understanding the user problem and defining the right approach through to delivery, measurement, and improvement.Design and build scalable backend systems, including APIs, data models, workflows, and infrastructure for complex enterprise products.Build and ship applied AI/LLM features, such as LLM chains, RAG systems, tool-using agents, structured-output pipelines, and evaluation workflowsCreate reusable, extensible platform building blocks that support multiple user journeys and reporting workflows rather than solving each problem in isolation.Improve the robustness of our systems, strengthening reliability, testing, observability, performance, and maintainability as we scale.Work directly with users, product, and data, using qualitative feedback and product data to understand the real problem and evaluate whether a solution works.Prototype and test new AI capabilities, turning promising ideas into practical product improvements that accelerate our roadmap.Bring thoughtful opinions and constructive challenge, helping the team make better product and technical decisions.Collaborate closely with other engineers, including through pair programming, technical design discussions, and shared problem-solving.Your profileTechnical requirementsStrong professional backend engineering experience, with a track record of designing and shipping reliable production systems.Experience in a small, high-ownership product team, ideally within a startup or scale-up engineering organisation of roughly 5–20 engineers.Evidence that you have shipped meaningful products end to end, rather than owning only a narrow component within a much larger organisation.Strong experience in Python (or another modern backend language such as Java, Ruby, or TypeScript, combined with the ability and willingness to become productive in Python quickly).Strong API, database, and systems design skills, with the ability to model complex workflows and build maintainable foundations for enterprise products.Applied AI/LLM experience: you have experience or a strong interest in LLM-powered features, ideally involving RAG or retrieval, tool use, agents, structured outputs, or evaluation systems.A solid software-quality mindset, including testing, code review, CI/CD, observability, and pragmatic approaches to reliability and security.Cloud and container experience, with an understanding of how to deploy, operate, and scale production workloads.Fluent English (C1+), both written and spoken. Nice to haveExperience building workflow, reporting, questionnaire, or other complex B2B SaaS products.Familiarity with backend technologies such as FastAPI, PostgreSQL, background queues Any experience with LangChain, LangSmith, or other LLM frameworksDeeper experience with RAG, retrieval, agents, LLM evaluation, and production AI systems.Experience improving latency, cost, and reliability for AI workloads.Knowledge of ESG, sustainability, climate tech, or corporate reporting.German language skills.Who you areKind and collaborative: You treat people well, communicate clearly, and help create a supportive, low-ego team Il s'attache ainsi à apporter des solutions nouvelles en matière d'analyse, de modélisation et d'évaluation environnementale des systèmes industriels et territoriaux dans un double contexte d'industrie des futurs et de villes et territoires soutenables.🏠 Contexte Présentation du sujetLe changement climatique met en lumière, comme l'a fait auparavant la crise COVID, les vulnérabilités et liens de dépendance généralisée de nos modes de vie envers les infrastructures, les chaînes de valeur, et modes d'organisation économique et technique, éléments souvent déconnectés de l'usager final, de ses besoins et des conditions d'occupation. Pour le secteur du bâtiment, Cimerman (2023) évoque une tendance depuis plusieurs décennies de « simplification cartésienne » de la conception et de l'opération du bâti. Celle-ci se traduit notamment par le développement d'un imaginaire de « bâtiment-machine », se traduisant par une superposition d'éléments techniques complexes (chauffage, ventilation, climatisation), susceptibles d'être pilotés au travers d'outils informatiques et d'une gestion centralisée optimisée (Cimerman, 2023).Face aux enjeux posés par le changement climatique, deux voies opposées d'adaptation du bâti se dessinent. La première, actuellement dominante, consiste à prolonger cet imaginaire de « bâtiment-machine », rationalisable, mesurable et optimisable, et ce notamment au travers du développement du « smart-building ». Cette approche technosolutionniste apporte des réponses clés-en-main (capteurs, outils de pilotage centralisés, etc.) aux gestionnaires et usagers de bâtiments. Néanmoins, elle présente certains défis pour leur maintenance et leur entretien. Nous pouvons citer le recours massif aux nouvelles technologies, coûteuses, complexes, rapidement obsolètes et dont la fabrication repose en grande partie sur des ressources finies. Cela pose de plus les questions centrales des compétences, de la délégation du savoir et des outils associés à des opérateurs experts externes.En contrepoint à la première voie, une seconde approche, encore marginale, émerge : celle d'un « bâtiment low-tech ». Popularisée ces dernières années en France par Philippe Bihouix (Bihouix, 2014), la low-tech questionne le rapport à la technologie et aux différentes formes de dépendances qu'elle génère (Tanguy et al., 2023). Dans le secteur du bâtiment, l'application de cette démarche renvoie souvent à la dépendance à la ressource (énergie et matière) : repenser les usages, l'origine des matériaux (réemployés, biosourcés) ou encore la simplicité de l'équipement utilisé. Bien que nécessaires, ces travaux s'intéressent pourtant peu à d'autres formes de dépendances associées à la technique, au titre desquelles nous pouvons citer la dépendance aux savoirs et aux formes d'organisation sociale et économique qui conditionnent l'adéquation, la pérennité et l'efficacité des solutions proposées.Cette thèse offre ainsi une immersion concrète dans les questions d'adaptation du parc bâti au changement climatique par la «&nbsp

column10: Tanguy et al., 2023). Appliquée au bâtiment, cette littérature reste toutefois majoritairement centrée sur la phase de conception et sur la dépendance à la ressource : sobriété énergétique, choix de matériaux biosourcés ou réemployés, réduction du niveau d'équipement technique.Deux angles morts en découlent. Le premier concerne la phase d'exploitation : la maintenance et l'entretien, qui représentent pourtant l'essentiel de la durée de vie d'un bâtiment et conditionnent la performance réelle des solutions installées, sont peu traités comme objet de recherche à part entière. Le second concerne la nature même des dépendances étudiées. Au-delà de la ressource, la conduite d'une opération de maintenance mobilise des savoirs et savoir-faire, des outils de diagnostic, des pièces détachées, des prestataires et des chaînes d'approvisionnement, ainsi que des cadres contractuels et réglementaires. Ces dépendances d’ordres cognitives, organisationnelles, économiques restent largement implicites et sous développées dans les travaux existants.La caractérisation de ces dépendances soulève par ailleurs une question d'échelle. Analysée au seul niveau du bâtiment, la maintenance apparaît comme une somme d'opérations techniques

column15: Ce que nous attendons de vousDémarche de la thèseL'objectif principal de cette thèse est de caractériser les apports d'une approche low-tech pour cartographier et maîtriser, sinon réduire, les différentes formes de dépendances associées à la maintenance et à l'entretien des bâtiments.Les dépendances analysées s'appuieront sur les techniques, pratiques, outils et réseaux en lien avec la maintenance qui seront mis en évidence dans les deux autres thèses du projet PERENNIS. Cette thèse s'inscrit donc en complète continuité de ces deux travaux.Dans un premier temps, il s'agira de construire un cadre d'analyse des dépendances liées à la maintenance du bâtiment, articulant quatre registres : les ressources (énergie, matière, pièces détachées), les savoirs et savoir-faire, les acteurs et leurs relations contractuelles, et les réseaux techniques et logistiques. Cette phase s'appuiera sur une revue de la littérature scientifique et « grise », sur un benchmark des pratiques et outils de maintenance existants, et sur des entretiens avec les acteurs du secteur (gestionnaires de patrimoine, bailleurs, mainteneurs, bureaux d'études, collectivités).Dans un deuxième temps, ce cadre sera mobilisé pour caractériser et rendre visibles les schémas de dépendance à l'échelle urbaine, sur un ou plusieurs territoires d'étude. Il s'agira notamment d'identifier les sources de données mobilisables pour objectiver ces schémas, de qualifier les points de fragilité et d'apprécier leur variabilité selon les typologies de bâtiments et les configurations d'acteurs.Dans un troisième temps, des stratégies prospectives low-tech de maintenance et d'entretien seront proposées et instruites. Il s'agira de construire des scénarios contrastés, d'évaluer leur capacité à réduire la vulnérabilité technique, économique et sociale des opérations de maintenance dans un contexte d'adaptation au changement climatique, et d'en discuter la faisabilité et l'acceptabilité avec les parties prenantes concernées.Verrous scientifiques :Définition et opérationnalisation de la notion de dépendance appliquée à la maintenance du bâti, au-delà de la seule dépendance à la ressource (savoirs, acteurs, organisations, réseaux)Caractérisation et représentation de schémas de dépendance à l'échelle urbaine, à partir de données hétérogènes et partiellement indisponiblesÉvaluation prospective de stratégies low-tech en l'absence de retours d'expérience consolidés et de métriques établiesArticulation interdisciplinaire entre sciences de l'ingénieur et sciences humaines et sociales, et capacité à répliquer l'approche tout en visant la « parcimonie » des méthodes et modèlesObjectifs de développement durable rattachés :ODD 11 – Villes et communautés durables ·ODD 12 – Consommation et production responsablesODD 13 – Mesures relatives à la lutte contre les changements climatiques.  🔍 Ce que nous recherchonsFormation : Bac +5 en ingénierie généraliste, sciences de l'environnement, génie civil ou énergétique du bâtiment, géographie/aménagement, ou discipline connexe. Une formation ou une sensibilité aux sciences humaines et sociales (sociologie des techniques, STS, économie de la fonctionnalité) serait un plus.Compétences requises :Méthodes qualitatives : conduite et analyse d'entretiens semi-directifs, observation de terrain, analyse de corpus documentaires.Analyse systémique et prospective : capacité à représenter un système sociotechnique, à construire et instruire des scénarios.Connaissance du bâtiment : compréhension du fonctionnement technique du bâti et de ses équipements, et des logiques d'exploitation et de maintenance.Traitement de données : aisance avec des données hétérogènes issues de sources variées

That repetition is where the energy goes, and it is part of why data-centre demand is now visible at grid scale: the Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory puts US data-centre electricity use at 176 TWh in 2023, 4.4 % of national consumption, a figure that more than doubled since 2017 largely because of AI servers, and projects 325–580 TWh by 2028. Emerging hardware attacks exactly this primitive: analog in-memory computing, silicon photonics, ferroelectric devices and stochastic computing perform the underlying matrix–vector products at lower energy than digital CMOS, under conditions on scale and precision, but return a perturbed result. The usual objection is that nobody can say in advance how much perturbation a model tolerates. In EMMA, this opportunity is pursued through a PCM-based photonic matrix–vector engine as the primary demonstrator, complemented where appropriate by FeFET-based analog computing, so that device-level non-idealities are treated as explicit design parameters rather than as after-the-fact implementation losses. Diffusion models are an unusual case in which that question has a mathematical answer: their convergence theory bounds the discrepancy between the generated and target distributions by three terms, of which only one, the L 2 error of the learned score, depends on the hardware. That side is now in good shape: for stochastic samplers, bounds linear in the dimension under minimal assumptions on the data

column1: expert-assurance-courtage-ia-at-panora-backed-by-hexa-paris-239581,Hexa,Expert Assurance | Courtage & IA @Panora (backed by Hexa),Paris,False,1790311202,"À propos de PanoraPanora est une plateforme d'IA native pour les courtiers en assurance. Nos agents IA automatisent les workflows à forte friction, cotation, comparaison de contrats, analyse des garanties, vérification de conformité, génération de documents et produisent des résultats structurés et actionnables en quelques minutes plutôt qu'en heures.Nous accompagnons les cabinets de courtage en France et en Belgique, avec une conviction claire : le courtage en assurance est opérationnellement dysfonctionnel depuis des décennies, et l'IA est enfin le bon outil pour y remédier. L'IA n'est plus optionnelle pour les courtiers : elle devient le standard. La question n'est plus si, mais à quel point elle est bien mise en œuvre.Panora a été fondée par Diane et Fabian. Diane a passé plusieurs années en capital-risque avec une solide expérience opérationnelle et connaît de l'intérieur les défis du scaling de business complexes. Fabian est un fondateur multi-récidiviste et ingénieur IA orienté produit, pionnier dans la construction de systèmes IA qui fonctionnent vraiment en production. Ensemble, ils ont décidé de créer Panora pour transformer les opérations d'assurance en avantage concurrentiel en temps réel pour les courtiers.Panora est soutenue par Hexa (anciennement eFounders), le studio de startups pionnier en Europe, qui a lancé plus de 35 entreprises dont des licornes comme Front, Aircall et Spendesk.Pourquoi ce rôle existeNous avons construit une IA qui lit des contrats, compare des garanties et génère des analyses de couverture à grande échelle. La technologie fonctionne. Nous avons maintenant besoin de quelqu'un qui la rende brillante : quelqu'un d'assez méticuleux pour détecter chaque lacune, d'assez expérimenté pour savoir ce qui compte vraiment dans une police, et d'assez curieux pour vouloir façonner l'IA de l'intérieur.Vous serez le cerveau assurance de Panora, la personne qui examine ce que notre IA produit, vérifie chaque synthèse, et réinjecte son expertise dans le système pour qu'il s'améliore en continu. C'est une opportunité unique de vivre la transformation par l'IA de l'intérieur et de participer activement à la construction du futur du courtage.Vos responsabilitésVérification des outputs IA, contrat par contrat. Vous examinez les synthèses, analyses de couverture et recommandations générées par notre IA. Vous vérifiez leur exactitude, corrigez les erreurs et garantissez que chaque output répond au niveau d'exigence qu'un courtier engagerait sa réputation à défendre. Votre œil méticuleux est la dernière ligne de défense avant que les outputs n'atteignent les clients.La boucle de feedback qui rend notre IA plus intelligente. Vous identifiez les schémas dans ce que l'IA réussit et rate. Vous travaillez avec les équipes produit et engineering pour réinjecter votre expertise assurance dans le système — améliorer les prompts, affiner le raisonnement, encoder les nuances que seules des années d'expérience permettent de saisir.Accompagnement client et confiance. Vous soutenez l'onboarding des clients et leur usage au quotidien, en aidant les courtiers à comprendre et faire confiance aux outputs de l'IA. Quand des questions surgissent, vous apportez la crédibilité et l'expertise nécessaires pour expliquer, rassurer ou corriger.Expertise assurance en IARD et Santé. Vous apportez une expertise approfondie en assurance dommages (IARD) et en assurance santé : les deux piliers de notre produit actuel. Vous en maîtrisez les spécificités et garantissez que notre IA traite les deux avec précision.Votre profilExpérience en tant que courtier, souscripteur, ou dans un rôle d'analyse technique des couverturesExpertise approfondie en IARD et/ou santé : vous connaissez ces produits sur le bout des doigtsMéticuleux de nature : vous êtes la personne qui repère l'exclusion enfouie page 47Vous lisez un contrat et identifiez immédiatement ce qui compte, ce qui manque, et ce qui pourrait nuire à un clientVous écrivez clairement et savez expliquer des concepts complexes d'assurance à des non-expertsVous êtes sincèrement curieux de ce que l'IA change pour notre secteur, enthousiaste à l'idée de le vivre de l'intérieur et d'y contribuerVous êtes à l'aise dans l'ambiguïté et attachez plus d'importance au métier de l'assurance qu'au confort de la routineFrançais courant

column1: senior-software-engineer-platform-infrastructure-berlin-375070,Holoplot,Senior Software Engineer - Platform & Infrastructure (f/m/d),Berlin,False,1790388591,"The product you will work onThe HOLOPLOT Matrix Array is a new type of sound system built around precise, software-defined control of sound in three dimensions - grounded in physics and implemented through a combination of custom hardware and purpose-built software. HOLOPLOT deployed Matrix Arrays in various venues, including the Sphere in Las Vegas - the world’s most advanced entertainment venue and, notably, home to the world’s largest audio installation in entertainment. Audio processing in HOLOPLOT systems is distributed: every loudspeaker runs embedded Linux, and hundreds of them have to be configured, coordinated, monitored, and updated as one system. This is enabled by multiple open source and in-house developed services running on an on-premises Kubernetes cluster. AWS-hosted services connect venues to remote monitoring, telemetry, and configuration. Many venues are air-gapped or only intermittently connected for remote servicing, and that constraint shapes most of the design decisions in the platform.The ideal candidate isWe are looking for a Senior Software Engineer who builds the platform our sound systems run on, and who takes responsibility for how it behaves in production.This is a software engineering role first. column1: system-software-engineer-gn-cloud-simulation-dresden-405805,Wandelbots GmbH,System Software Engineer (gn) Cloud & Simulation,Dresden,False,1790377792,"Your missionAt Wandelbots, we are building NOVA, a platform that makes industrial robot programming accessible to everyone. Our Simulation team develops the technologies that allow partners, customers, and internal teams to work with photorealistic digital twins of real production environments.This includes a pipeline that transforms real-world scans into usable 3D scenes through Gaussian Splatting, as well as a browser-based streaming platform built on NVIDIA Omniverse and Isaac Sim. Both technologies work today, but neither is yet operated as a product. Your mission is to change that.The first step is internal standardization. We want to replace individually maintained environments and hand-crafted deployments with one reproducible, documented solution that teams can use independently: scene in, session out, without requiring the Simulation team to operate every setup.The second step is external productization. Chez Doctrine, nous construisons le leader de l’IA juridique en Europe.

Notre conviction ? Le droit ne doit pas être ralenti par des tâches répétitives. Il doit être augmenté par une IA spécialisée, conçue pour comprendre, analyser et produire du raisonnement juridique avec un haut niveau d’exigence.
Notre ambition ? Permettre aux professionnels du droit de gagner en fiabilité, en efficacité et en sérénité, grâce à une plateforme unique, exhaustive et sécurisée.
Aujourd’hui, 27 000 professionnels du droit, répartis dans cinq pays (France, Italie, Allemagne, Espagne, Luxembourg), nous font confiance.
Notre développement est guidé par une approche claire : une vision globale, ancrée dans une compréhension fine des spécificités locales.
Derrière cette ambition, une équipe d’environ 250 personnes, réunies autour d’un même objectif : accompagner les juristes et avocats à toutes les étapes de leur travail, de l’analyse à la rédaction.
Et nous n’en sommes qu’au début.
Les cabinets d’avocats indépendants représentent le segment qui connaît la plus forte croissance chez Doctrine, avec une hausse de 50 % sur les 12 derniers mois.

column9: Et vous, prêt·e à innover à nos côtés ?🎯 Ce que nous attendons de vousEn tant que chercheur postdoctoal, vous êtes au cœur de nos missions en recherche et innovation affecté au centre SPIN. Au sein de ce centre vous conjuguez curiosité scientifique avec un intérêt pour l’articulation entre problématiques de recherche fondamentale et problématiques indus-trielles.Le centre SPIN est l’un des centres de recherche de Mines Saint-Etienne dédié à la recherche en génie des procédés et rassemble environ 80 personnes comprenant enseignants-chercheurs, postdocs, doctorants, stagiaires, et profite du soutien de personnels administratifs et techniques. L’activité du centre SPIN s’inscrit dans le périmètre du Laboratoire Georges Friedel (UMR 5307) et du Laboratoire Environnement Ville et Société (UMR 5600). Vous développerez votre activité de recherche au sein du département « Procédés de Manipulation de la Matière Granulaire » (PMMG) qui concentre divers expertises scientifiques sur les procédés de transformation et la caractérisa-tion de matériaux granulaires à partir d’approches expérimentales et numériques, ainsi qu’à travers différents champs disciplinaires allant de la géométrie mathématique à la chimie minérale en pas-sant par la physique des écoulements complexes. L’activité du centre SPIN, comme du départe-ment PMMG, est caractérisée par une forte interdisciplinarité ainsi que par de nombreuses collabo-rations avec d’autres institutions de recherche et d’enseignement en Europe et dans le monde, et profite de nombreux contrats avec des partenaires industriels.La matière granulaire est un état de la matière particulier qui peine à être décrit par les lois de com-portement qui s’appliquent habituellement aux fluides, ou aux solides. Cependant une vaste majo-rité des matières premières transformées dans de nombreux secteurs industriels, ou des produits manufacturés, se présentent sous la forme de particules solides (grains de poudre, agglomérats, granulés, comprimés, etc..). La complexité de la dynamique de ces solides divisés émerge du grand nombre de particules solides concernées. En particulier dans le cas de particules solides transpor-tées dans une conduite de transport pneumatique, où l’écoulement d’un gaz le long d’une con-duite entraine les particules solides, les interactions avec les parois solides sont le siège de nom-breux procédés physico-chimiques. Au-delà des collisions élastiques qui entraînent le rebond de la majorité des particules solides sur les parois, des processus de fragmentation, d’arrachement de charges, d’échauffement local, etc. sont susceptibles de provoquer des transformations de la ma-tière transportée. Dans certains cas, la formation de dépôts sur les parois peut être observée et affecte négativement les performances du procédé de transport.Le travail attendu sera de mettre en place un montage expérimental capable d’étudier les proces-sus responsables de la formation de ces enrochements à partir de mesures de pression, de débit, de charges électrostatiques, d’observation par microscopie, de caractérisation granulométrique etc. Différentes poudres modèles pourront être utilisées afin de reproduire les observations d’enrochement reportées dans la litérature. column1: phd-inverse-modal-identification-of-free-field-radiated-noise-from-unducted-rotor-stator-stages-from-laboratory-arrays-to-open-fan-flight-tests-ecu-171367,Centrale Innovation,PhD - Inverse modal identification of free-field radiated noise from unducted rotor-stator stages: from laboratory arrays to Open Fan flight tests,"Ecully, Auvergne-Rhône-Alpes, France",False,1790245804,"Context:This postdoctoral position is part of the European project TAKE-OFF (Clean Aviation programme), which is preparing the full-scale flight demonstration of Safran Aircraft Engines’ RISE Open Fan engine on the Airbus A380 flying testbed, with the aim of reducing fuel consumption by 30 % and entering service around 2035. Without a nacelle, the engine noise sources radiate directly into free field. LMFA (École Centrale de Lyon), in collaboration with LVA (INSA Lyon), is in charge of analysing the near-field pressure data acquired in flight by microphones installed on the fuselage, in order to reconstruct the engine noise sources.Objective:To extend the modal analysis methods developed at LMFA for ducted engines [1] to unducted fans. For the first time, modal analysis will be applied to microphones located in an unconfined medium and to modes radiating under free-field conditions, and design criteria specific to this configuration will be established (spatial sampling, resolution, array-to-rotor distance relative to the array size).Description:Task 1 – Model and inverse problem. Build a set of eigenfunctions describing the radiation of an unducted rotor-stator stage (spinning modes weighted by Bessel functions [2], spherical harmonics, etc.) and embed it in a Bayesian inverse approach [1] to estimate the modal amplitudes of tonal and broadband components. Flow and fuselage effects may be accounted for through CAA computations.Task 2 – Validation on the MAMBO database. The developments will be tested on an unducted propeller + stator configuration recently studied at LMFA (MAMBO project), instrumented with three arrays: a half-cylindrical array, a planar array on the side (representative of fuselage instrumentation) and a motorised arc array measuring directivity, which will serve as an independent reference. This study will assess the robustness of the method and define array design criteria.Task 3 – Application to flight tests. column1: customer-success-manager-emea-67837,TRM Labs,Customer Success Manager,EMEA,False,1790358004,"Build a Safer World.TRM Labs provides AI-powered intelligence solutions that help public and private sector agencies investigate and disrupt crime. TRM's platforms enable investigators to trace illicit activity, build cases, and construct operating pictures of threat networks. Leading agencies and businesses worldwide rely on TRM to make the world safer and more secure.The AI Customer Success function is being built from the ground up, and this role will help define it internationally. As the first Customer Success Manager in this area, you will own the end-to-end post-sale experience for a portfolio of customers that includes some of the world’s most sophisticated cyber threat intelligence teams and investigators, national security agencies, and financial crime teams. Your mandate is not just to manage accounts—you will help establish the playbook, define what success looks like, and drive a product-led growth motion that turns new customers into long-term, expanding partners.The impact you will have:Build and ship a v1 onboarding playbook within the first 30 days—a practical, working version built from early customer engagements that can be iterated as you learn what drives adoption across international customer segments.Use AI to build production CS workflows that pull from ChurnZero, Salesforce, Gong, and product usage telemetry to auto-generate account health summaries and QBR drafts—compressing hours of reporting preparation into minutes so you can spend your time on the work that actually requires human judgment.Define and track adoption benchmarks across the portfolio—hands-on-keyboard usage, consumption rates, and account-specific success metrics—and surface at-risk accounts before renewal decisions are made.Identify and scope the highest-impact PLG play within 60 days by working backwards from expansion targets, focusing on the one or two use cases most likely to drive consumption across the customer base.Run executive business reviews and QBRs with senior stakeholders at government agencies and financial institutions internationally—building the trust and credibility that turns TRM from a vendor into a mission-critical partner.Partner with ADs on expansion plays, co-own NRR targets, and build the structured path to proving value for every customer with an expiring or at-risk contract.Close the feedback loop between customers and Product—synthesize adoption blockers, feature gaps, and new use-case opportunities into prioritized, actionable input that informs the roadmap.Design the CS infrastructure and tooling stack that scales as the product grows—you are building the foundation the next CSM hire will inherit.What we're looking for:Background in cyber or cyber threat intelligence, intelligence agencies, financial crime investigations, or regulatory and compliance environments.5+ years as an onboarding engineer, customer success manager, deployment strategist, or in another post-sale role with proven ownership of NRR, GRR, and expansion metrics—you have the track record, not just the title.Domain credibility in cyber, national security, or financial crime—you can walk into a room of investigators and earn their trust in the first meeting, not the fifth.Demonstrated zero-to-one builder experience—you have built a CS function, onboarding playbook, or PLG motion from scratch and can point to the specific outcomes it drove.Production AI fluency—you have built real, repeatable AI workflows, not just experiments, that synthesize data from multiple sources into outputs that run consistently and deliver measurable results. You can show the workflow, explain the data logic, and articulate where human judgment stays in the loop.A high level of independence—you set your own agenda, operate without needing constant direction, and ship v1 before you have all the answers.Strong executive presence—you can run a QBR with a senior government stakeholder or financial institution executive and command the room through substance, not just polish.Experience supporting international customers, with the ability to navigate regional, cultural, and time-zone differences.About the Team:This team focuses on TRM’s AI-driven Intel platform, supporting investigators and cyber teams working on complex cases involving cyber threats.This is the first Customer Success hire dedicated to international customers—you will help build the function from the ground up, with high autonomy, direct access to leadership, and meaningful influence on how TRM approaches customer success globally.The broader TRM CS organization operates distributed, not distant—async-first communication through Slack, strong documentation, and intentional synchronous time for key decisions.You will work directly with the Head of Customer Success and Patrick South, CRO, with close day-to-day collaboration with international Sales teams and Product.Team Operating Rhythms:As a globally distributed team, members work across multiple time zones. This role will primarily align its working hours and customer coverage with international markets, with flexibility to collaborate across regions when needed.Our Customer Success team is fully remote, thriving on asynchronous communication and collaboration through Slack channels and detailed documentation. We hold weekly customer syncs, biweekly health syncs, join our associated POD calls, and regularly engage with customers across international markets. As experts in our craft, we focus on providing support, driving value, and building meaningful relationships with our customers as trusted advisors. We are on the front lines of TRM, ensuring our customers get the most out of the product and bringing valuable insights back to the team.The team moves fast and iterates—v1 ships before it is perfect, and feedback is expected to be direct and specific.On-Call Responsibilities:End-to-End Ownership: While there is no formal hourly rotation, you will be the primary lead for your area and responsible for customer success across international markets. This requires a high degree of agency and a commitment to seeing mission-critical tasks through to resolution, including the flexibility to handle urgent needs outside of standard hours or on weekends when they arise.Learn about TRM Speed in this position:Within 30 days of joining, you ship a working v1 onboarding playbook built from your first 2–3 accounts—not a slide deck, but a live document with measurable adoption benchmarks that the account team is already using to set customer expectations.Within 6 weeks, you share a draft success-metrics framework at 50% complete with the account team and key customers to validate direction—getting real signal on what drives credit consumption before investing further in building out the full playbook.Within 60 days, you identify and scope the highest-impact PLG play by working backwards from expansion targets—presenting a concrete recommendation to leadership on which use case to prioritize and why, grounded in actual account data from international customers.Application InstructionsIf you’re interested in joining TRM, we encourage you to apply directly. Every application is reviewed by our Talent team.Before applying, review the job description carefully and highlight the experience and impact that best demonstrate the required qualifications. Please also provide thoughtful and accurate answers to the application questions, as these will be used to evaluate your qualifications for the role.If you send your resume directly to someone at TRM, we can’t guarantee it will reach the appropriate hiring team. Applying directly is the best way to ensure you’re considered.What to Expect From Our Interview Process Our process is designed to understand how you think, solve problems, and deliver impact, while giving you the opportunity to evaluate TRM. Most interview processes include a case study, AI skills assessment, and Leadership Principles interview.Recruiter Intro: Explore your experience, motivations, and alignment with the role.Hiring Manager: Dive deeper into your relevant experience, skills, and impact.First Round: Typically 1–2 interviews focused on the skills most critical to the role.Final Round: Typically 3–5 interviews to go deeper on your craft, problem-solving, and alignment with TRM.References: We’ll speak with former colleagues who can provide perspective on your work and impact.Offer: If it’s a mutual fit, your recruiter will walk you through your offer and answer your questions.Welcome to TRM: Once you sign, we’ll get you ready for your first day and onboarding.Your recruiter will share your specific interview plan and preparation guidance along the way.Learn more about interviewing at TRMLife at TRMWe are building a safer world. That promise shows up in how we work every day.TRM moves quickly. We are a high velocity, high ownership team that expects clarity, follow-through, and impact. People who thrive here are energized by hard problems, experimentation, and continuous feedback. If something takes months elsewhere, it will ship here in days.Our work sits at the intersection of AI, national security, and fighting crime. The problems are complex, the stakes are real, and the environment evolves quickly. The pace and intensity of the work reflect the importance of the mission. As a result, the way we operate requires a high level of ownership, adaptability, collaboration, and creative problem-solving.At TRM, you should expect:Priorities and targets to change quickly as we experiment and iterateWork that often requires operating with a high degree of ambiguityA high level of personal ownership and accountabilityClose collaboration across teams and functionsFrequent, high-touch communicationCreative problem solving and out-of-the-box thinkingA pace that rewards urgency, adaptability, and outcomesThis environment is energizing for people who enjoy building, solving hard problems, and making progress in situations that are not always fully defined. It also requires comfort navigating ambiguity, adjusting course as new information emerges, and maintaining focus and positivity in a fast-moving and intense environment.We also recognize that this style of operating is not for everyone. If you are primarily optimizing for predictability or a consistently balanced workload, we encourage you to use the interview process to pressure test whether this environment is truly the right fit. We want teammates who thrive here, not just survive here.At the same time, many people find this work deeply rewarding. If you are excited by meaningful problems, motivated by ambitious goals, and energized by working alongside mission-driven colleagues, there is a good chance you will find TRM to be an exceptional place to grow and contribute. Learn more about Interviewing at TRM  AI Fluency at TRMAI fluency is a baseline expectation at TRM.We believe AI meaningfully changes how top performers operate. We expect every team member to use AI to accelerate and reimagine their craft, not just automate surface tasks.At TRM, AI fluency means you are among the top 10 percent of operators in your function in how you apply AI to:Accelerate repeatable workflowsStructure and solve problemsImprove output qualityIncrease speed and leverageYou will be evaluated on applied AI fluency during the interview process.Leadership PrinciplesWe hire and grow against three leadership principles. They’re the standards for how we operate, treat each other, and make decisions.Impact-Oriented Trailblazer: We put customers first and move with speed, focus, and adaptability. We treat every plan like an experiment – test, ship, measure, and iterate quickly.Master Craftsperson: We care deeply about our craft. We balance speed with high standards, own outcomes end‑to‑end, and invest in getting better everyday.Inspiring Colleague: We add clarity and energy, not noise. We bring humility, candor, and a one‑team mindset — giving and receiving feedback to make the team stronger.Join our MissionAt TRM, we care deeply about our craft. We are looking for individuals who want their work to matter, who experiment with speed and rigor, and who take pride in building a safer world for billions of people. If you’re excited by TRM’s mission but don’t check every box, we encourage you to apply — we hire for slope, judgment, and the will to learn fast.TRM is a Series C company with $220M in total funding, backed by Goldman Sachs, Bessemer, Y Combinator, Thoma Bravo, and others. Headquartered in San Francisco, TRM operates as a distributed-first company with hubs in Los Angeles, San Francisco, New York, Washington D.C., London, and Singapore. column1: senior-business-intelligence-lead-all-genders-munchen-386242,Reev,Senior Business Intelligence Lead (all genders),München,False,1790312972,"Your MissionEV charging is evolving from a niche technology into everyday infrastructure. The goal is to establish clear definitions and consistent metrics so that teams and leadership can make informed decisions based on the same numbers. Someone who understands that unclear definitions, rather than a lack of data, are often the real problem can make a significant impact in this role. Check the results carefully. What this role is not You will not be the central owner of every dashboard request. column1: ResearchGate is the professional network for scientists and researchers. From climate change and emerging diseases to food security and the responsible development of AI, the challenges facing our world are complex. Still, we’re optimistic about the power of millions of scientists working together to tackle them. We provide scientists with the help and support they need by connecting them to the world’s most active scientific community.

We've built a platform that gives the world's scientists the tools and services they need to connect, collaborate, and advance their research. Over 25 million members from 193 countries use ResearchGate to share, discover, and discuss research.

We're looking for an enthusiastic frontend engineer with the skills and ability to turn great ideas into reality. You should have an in-depth understanding of current web technologies and front-end development, and be passionate about creating a great user experience. Your input will help us grow and maintain our React front-end.

Join a team that encourages you to explore, learn, and go beyond, while seeing your work lead to actionable results. Put your creative problem-solving and development skills into action and make a positive impact on science and society. This is a full-time position based in Germany.

You will be an integral part of the product team dedicated to enhancing ResearchGate's publisher-facing product. This role involves designing, constructing, and refining the platform to further our mission of facilitating global scientific connections and ensuring open access to research. At present, our team is working on making ResearchGate a great platform for publishers to connect with existing and future authors.

Your immediate colleagues will consist of JavaScript and PHP engineers, an Engineering Manager, a Product Manager, a UX Designer, and a UX Writer. Maintain and improve existing features and related infrastructure.
Collaborate with Product Managers, Designers, and Software Engineers to deliver compelling publisher-facing products.
5+ years frontend web development experience in TypeScript (React), CSS
Demonstrated ability to create code that is easily comprehensible, maintainable, and testable.
Eagerness to acquire new skills, delve into different technologies and programming languages, and a willingness to acknowledge areas where expertise may be lacking.
Approach problem-solving thoughtfully, embracing curiosity and maintaining an open-minded perspective.
You are comfortable incorporating AI-assisted development tools into your daily workflow and exercise strong engineering judgment when evaluating and refining their output.
It would be a plus if you already had knowledge of relational and document-based databases (we use MongoDB and Postgres).
You take responsibility over your own solutions and continuously improve them.
You engage in proactive and efficient communication within our distributed work environment.
You focus on building a great product.

You get mentorship, context, and access to everyone. You do not get someone assigning you tasks every morning. Take a rough problem statement, come back with an approach, show drafts while they can still change, and flag what is not working. What you bring should outweigh what it costs us to support you.Potential Research DirectionsThese are directions we could explore, with scope defined together at the start based on your background and where the work leads.1. column9: efficiency, harvest timing, raw material availability to craft a competitive costing environment where T2 and T3 suppliers are being challenged to provide transparent, and competitive pricing to achieve a win win supply chain for both Quince and our partners.&lt

column7: Success in this role means achieving material cost at or near should-costing, below market indices, securing supply continuity, and contributing to product excellence by aligning material procurement with the company’s innovation and sustainability goals. column11: Establish a monitoring framework to forecast global market shifts, raw material fluctuations, currency risks, and macro-material trends. Deliver actionable intelligence to procurement and leadership on a regular cadence.

column7: Build and operationalize a live tracking system for key raw material prices, currency movements, and supply risks to proactively surface threats and opportunities.&lt

column11: Construct and scale material-specific clean sheets to lock in baseline component costs before finished-goods production. Provide the costing foundation for Tier 1 negotiations.

column7: Build material-specific clean sheets for all top raw material inputs to create pricing transparency and support Tier 1 negotiation.&amp
Support Buy Plan margin review to govern company margin target.&amp
Partner with material sourcing team to ensure transparent, competitive pricing from all key material suppliers (we own material, we own costing)&amp

column13: Map and design an upstream network strategy to consolidate raw material volumes across key material types and maximize direct-to-mill leverage. Reduce supply chain complexity while improving cost and availability.&amp

column7: Complete mapping of the Tier 2 and Tier 3 vendor landscape and deliver a defined material and vendor strategy that reduces complexity, ensures capacity, and increases direct-to-mill buying power.&amp

Collaborate with cross-functional teams to integrate upstream material availability into product design and development cycles, ensuring early-stage cost optimization and seamless material-to-finished-good transitions.&amp

column13: Design and execute RFPs tailored specifically to raw material vendors, yarn spinners/mills, tanneries, and textile mills. Own the full bidding process from vendor outreach through award.&amp

column7: Consistently deliver product exceptional material cost without sacrificing product quality or ESG considerations&amp

Negotiate and execute immediate cost-reduction agreements directly with Tier 2 material suppliers, while simultaneously institutionalizing repeatable negotiation frameworks to build long-term material maturity and sustainable competitive advantage.&amp
Partner directly with the Material Sourcing, Product Sourcing and Tier 1 and Tier 2 vendors to align on, and implement, material benefits into finished goods costing.&amp

column11: Identify and execute on opportunities to reshape the supply chain and extract new financial value beyond traditional sourcing boundaries, including verticalization and volume consolidation plays.&amp

column7: E.g. How do we become a market maker for Cashmere, Silk, etc? Could we sell cashmere and silk to other retailers? Strong analytical and financial modeling skills

Dabei arbeitest du mit Teams aus Technologie, digitaler Kommunikationsberatung, Kreation, Content und UX zusammen.Du arbeitest eng mit unseren Kund:innen und interdisziplinären Projektteams zusammen, verstehst Anforderungen und Herausforderungen und übersetzt sie in konkrete Projektziele und Lösungen.Für dich endet Projektmanagement nicht mit der erfolgreichen Delivery: Du erkennst neue Bedarfe und Potenziale bei bestehenden Kund:innen und entwickelst Projekte und Kundenbeziehungen gemeinsam mit unseren Fachexpert:innen weiter.Du bringst deine Erfahrung und Projektperspektive in Angebote, Ausschreibungen und Pitches ein. column1: product-engineer-hamburg-hq-74436,Buying Labs Gmbh 1,Product Engineer (m/f/d),Hamburg HQ,False,1790291379,"Our Company ""Buying Labs is the leading global partner for sourcing and distributing premium consumer goods!""We're looking for a Product Engineer (m/f/d) to join our Tech team at Buying Labs ideally based in Hamburg or remotely for the right fit. In this role, you'll combine deep technical skill with strong product thinking to build tools and features using AI that create real value for our users and our business. You'll own features end to end - from scoping and design through development, deployment, and adoption - and use AI to build smarter and faster at every step.This is a role for builders who care about impact: people who understand both the user perspective and the underlying business processes, who can scope what needs to be built and then make it happen.Your MissionEnd-to-End Product Delivery: Own features from concept to production and real users, not just code -ship complete solutions that drive measurable business value. Scope requirements, define technical approaches, and deliver across frontend and backend, with quality built in from the start and verified through appropriate testing.Product Thinking &amp
column2: User Focus: Understand user needs and business processes to identify what should be built and why. Translate product ideas and stakeholder input into shipped experiences that users actually adopt.Building AI into Products: Design and integrate AI-powered features into our platform - not just using coding assistants, but building AI solutions that solve real problems for our users. Identify opportunities where AI can speed up workflows, improve decision-making, or unlock new capabilities.Data Modelling &amp
column3: Scalable Systems: Build solid data models and scalable architectures that serve as a reliable foundation for our products. Turn repeated work into shared building blocks (UI components, data import flows, AI pipelines) so each new tool is faster to build than the last.Stakeholder Collaboration &amp
column4: Adoption: Work with stakeholders at all levels - from leadership to operations - to align on priorities and drive adoption of new tools and features. Communicate technical concepts clearly and build buy-in for your solutions across the organisation.Continuous Improvement: Gather feedback early, iterate quickly, and continuously improve what you build. Stay current with emerging technologies and engineering best practices to keep our tools &amp
column5: systems ahead of what the business needs to keep the platform competitive.Nice to Have:Experience with LLM tooling — provider APIs (Anthropic, OpenAI, Gemini), agent and tool-use patterns (MCP), and evaluating output quality.Familiarity with vector search technologies (pgvector or similar).Hands-on experience with product analytics and observability tools (e.g. PostHog, Sentry) to measure usage and drive adoption.Experience integrating ERPs or operational systems (orders, inventory, master data).Background in eCommerce, wholesale, or B2B platform environments.Python for data tooling
column6: Docker, GitHub Actions, AWS.Your ProfileBachelor's degree or equivalent experience in Computer Science, Engineering, or a related field.5–8 years of professional experience in software development with a strong product mindsetStrong experience with TypeScript and modern React. head-of-engineering-berlin-293141,Moss,Head of Engineering (f/m/d),Berlin,False,1790282406,"At Moss, we give finance professionals the power to automate their day-to-day and make forward-thinking decisions.Our culture is what makes that possible: we play to win, we obsess over quality, and we win as One Moss, and it works. Moss closed a €35 million Series C in August 2026, crossing a €1 billion valuation, and became one of Europe's fintech unicorns. Join us for what's next.We're hiring a Head of Engineering to lead engineering for one of our product tribes. You'll manage 15 to 20 engineers directly, with tech leads in each squad owning technical direction but no management layer between you and the team. You report to the CTO and sit in a tribe leadership trio with the Product Tribe Lead and Design Lead. Which tribe you'd lead is something we'll work out with you during the process.This is a people leadership role with a hard technical requirement. The engineers report to you, so hiring, development, performance and pace are yours. At the same time you have to hold your own on system architecture: challenge estimates from your engineers, spar with the Product Tribe Lead on solutions, and know when a design is wrong before it ships. This role needs both.How we're set upTribes are the organisational body: people management, capacity, planning and reporting live there. Squads are assigned to problem spaces and run discovery and delivery, each led by a trio of Tech Lead, Product Manager and Product Designer. Tech Leads own the technical decisions in their squad, including estimates, and write code alongside their engineers. They don't manage people. You do.We keep the structure deliberately flat. Management is anchored at tribe level, squad composition flexes to serve the most important work, and structure changes as we learn (roughly every six months in practice, not on a schedule). Discovery and delivery run in parallel: the next mission is scoped before engineers finish the current one, so engineers weigh in on architecture early and have the context to unblock themselves.What you'll ownFeasibility and delivery for the tribe. You're accountable for tribe-wide delivery outcomes and velocity: the right problems, solved at the right quality, as fast as possible.The people. 15 to 20 direct reports. Hiring, onboarding, expectations, feedback, development, compensation and promotion recommendations, and the tough calls that keep talent density high. Tech Leads feed you performance signals

column1: senior-product-designer-berlin-402706,Secfix,Senior Product Designer,Remote - Europe,False,1790271611,"Senior Product Designer @ SecfixLocation: Remote (EMEA) · CET/CEST time zoneHi — I'm Grigory, co-founder and CTO at Secfix.How do you feel about owning a feature from the first customer conversation to the version that's live in production — writing the spec yourself, pairing closely with engineers through the build, and overseeing your design shipped in production exactly the way you designed it? If that sounds like the right shape of the job — designer who owns, not designer who hands off — read on.I've spent most of my career believing the best designers aren't the ones with the prettiest Figma files. They're the ones who can frame a problem, write a spec, sit with engineers through the build, and own that what shipped is what they designed. Our founding product designer, Ghada, has been doing exactly that since we started. The engineering team has doubled, and we're shipping faster than we ever have. We're hiring the third designer because there's more good work to do than two people can handle — and we'd rather ship faster than slow down.Why Secfix existsOver 1.78 million SMBs in Europe need to comply with security frameworks — ISO 27001, GDPR, TISAX, SOC 2 — just to sell to enterprise customers. The process is manual, painful, and takes over a year. We automated it.Our platform integrates with a company's full tech stack — AWS, Azure AD, Jira, GitLab, GCP, and more — automatically extracts compliance evidence, and guides teams to certification in weeks instead of months. Our fastest customer was certified in 4 weeks instead of the industry-standard 12+ months.We've raised €17M in total (€12M Series A), backed by Alstin Capital, Neosfer (Commerzbank), and Bayern Capital. We're on a profitable trajectory, growing fast, and building the team that will take us to European market leadership.This space is not threatened by AI
column2: it's amplified by it. Compliance requires deep domain expertise combined with automation. Our new AI product (CISO AI) is just getting started, and there's a huge amount of product design work ahead: agentic workflows, intelligent evidence collection, context-aware policy generation, and more.What we believeCompliance software has historically been built like the audit it automates — heavy, defensive, ugly. We're building something else. The customer is a real person trying to ship audit-ready evidence on a Friday afternoon. The product should respect their time, automate the boring parts, and make the rest feel calm.Quality is the product. Most of our category competes on feature lists. We compete on craft. A clear empty state, a sync that doesn't lie, a settings page that holds together at eleven permission tiers — these are the things customers feel before they can name them. Design at Secfix is not what wraps the product. It's most of what makes it work.What the role isWe expect strong design skills, strong product thinking, and the ability to hold your own in a technical discussion. You work in a small team — usually with one or two engineers — and pair closely from the first prototype through to production. You own the project from beginning to end.Alongside the features you ship, you do three things that make everyone else faster:Maintain the components and patterns that make design fast.Own how the team ships. We have no PMs. You write the specs, run the ticketing workflow, keep engineers unblocked.Build the tools and skills — Cursor rules, design QA skills, prompt templates — that let engineers do good design work without you in the room.The leverage is doing all four well. Doing only one is the wrong shape.How we workNo PMs. Designers and engineers run product. You talk to customers, frame the problem, write the spec, decide what ships.Small temporary teams. You plus one or two engineers per project. Whoever is closest to the problem leads.Design leads the logic
column3: engineering tests feasibility. You bring the V1. Engineers push back on what's expensive or risky, and start ahead with system design. They help spot edge cases. You adjust it fast. We get from v1 to v4 in a matter of hours or a few days.Prototype-grade, not wireframes. Real components, real states, real copy. Sometimes an LLM-built prototype before Figma. column1: product-engineer-munchen-430794,Lpe Immobilien Management Gmbh,Product Engineer (m/w/d),München,False,1790258963,"Warum LPE Immobilien?Die Hausverwaltung ist der unterschätzteste Beruf Deutschlands: Kein anderer entscheidet so unmittelbar darüber, wie Menschen wohnen. Trotzdem gilt der Hausverwalter bis heute als Buchhalter mit Schlüsselbund. Wir digitalisieren unsere eigenen Prozesse, um die Arbeit unserer Verwalter jeden Tag ein Stück besser zu machen, mit dem Anspruch, die Branche zu revolutionieren.Kaum eine Branche wurde von moderner Software so lange übersehen. Der Abstand zwischen dem, was ist, und dem, was möglich ist, ist riesig, und wir bauen ihn Stück für Stück zu. Du wärst eine der ersten Personen im Produktteam.Was dich bei uns erwartet – Deine AufgabenDu entwickelst Fullstack in TypeScript, vom Kundenportal über das Verwaltercockpit bis zu den Services und der Infrastruktur dahinter, auf der grünen Wiese und ohne Altlasten. Features verantwortest du end-to-end: von der Idee über die Gestaltung bis zum Release, bei Bedarf auch ohne Designer an deiner Seite.Du baust KI-Agenten als Produktfunktionalität für unsere Verwalter und Kunden.
